blocks.text: The axon terminal of the presynaptic neuron has several synaptic knobs containing many synaptic vesicles packed with chemicals called neurotransmitters. Passing an action potential's information across the synapse is synaptic transmission.

items: The action potential arrives at the synaptic knobs and calcium gates in the presynaptic membrane open.
Calcium ions diffuse rapidly from the cleft into the presynaptic axon.
The calcium makes the synaptic vesicles fuse with the membrane and release neurotransmitter by exocytosis.
The neurotransmitter diffuses across the cleft and binds to receptor proteins on the postsynaptic membrane.
This binding acts as a message: Na+ gates in the postsynaptic membrane open and an action potential is generated there.
The neurotransmitter does not stay in the cleft: at many synapses it is reabsorbed by the presynaptic neuron, at others broken down by enzymes.

blocks.alt: A presynaptic axon terminal on the left full of vesicles of neurotransmitter, a narrow cleft, and a postsynaptic cell on the right with receptor proteins. Ca2+ enters the terminal, neurotransmitter is released into the cleft, binds to the receptors, and Na+ enters the postsynaptic cell to start a new impulse. Six numbered steps are listed below.
blocks.caption: Structure of a synapse and the mechanism of synaptic transmission (original diagram after Figure 15.7).
blocks.long_description: When an action potential reaches the synaptic knobs, calcium gates open and Ca2+ diffuses in from the cleft. This makes the synaptic vesicles fuse with the membrane and release neurotransmitter by exocytosis. The neurotransmitter diffuses across the cleft and binds to receptor proteins on the postsynaptic membrane, whose Na+ gates open so an action potential starts there. Afterwards the transmitter is reabsorbed by the presynaptic neuron or broken down by enzymes.

blocks.title: More impulses, more transmitter
blocks.text: The higher the frequency of action potentials in the presynaptic axon, the more neurotransmitter is released.
